chunks: Shall I be content with myself that it is said, '[This is] the Commander of the Believers,'
although I do not share with them the hardships of the world, or shall I be an example for them in the distresses of life?
I have not been created to keep myself busy in eating good foods, like the tied animal whose only worry is its fodder, or the loose animal whose activity is to swallow,
it fills its belly with its feed and is distracted from the purpose behind it,
or shall I be left uncontrolled to pasture freely, or neglected aimlessly, or draw the rope of misguidance, or roam aimlessly in the paths of bewilderment!
ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about the true meaning of being 'Amir al-Mu'minin'?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs a vivid rhetorical question to critique the materialism of the Umayyad elite, contrasting their beast-like preoccupation with sustenance against the leader's duty to share in the 'hardships of time' (makarih al-dahr). This reflects the Shia principle of *Zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere withdrawal, but as active solidarity with the people, rejecting both aimless luxury and arbitrary rule. The text underscores the moral imperative for leaders to avoid *istisfa'* (self-aggrandizement) and remain grounded in the realities of their subjects' lives.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Shall I be content with being called ‘Amīr al-mu’minīn’ (The Commander of the Believers),
although I do not share with the people the hardships of the world? Or shall I be an example for them in the distresses of life?
I have not been created to keep myself busy in eating good foods like the tied animal whose only worry is his fodder or like a loose animal whose activity is to swallow.
It fills its belly with its feed and forgets the purpose behind it.
Shall I be left uncontrolled to pasture freely, or draw the rope of misguidance or roam aimlessly in the paths of bewilderment?
